rv.q: Between the musical's powerful content and Doyle's inventive presentation, 'Assassins' is still a killer show.
As scattershot as this production sometimes seems, however, it hits enough targets to draw blood.
The show isn’t a flawless revival, but it’s so perfectly suited to the moment that quibbles about anemic staging and singing can wait.
Classic Stage Company's new revival elevates “Assassins” to the top tier of Stephen Sondheim’s many musicals.
The Classic Stage Company revival of Assassins , Stephen Sondheim and John Weidman's musical about the killers and attempted killers of American presidents, is that kind of show.
Missing this show would be a shame — if you can snag a ticket.
With a fresh urgency, an extraordinary cast, and a characteristically unshowy staging, it is a thrilling return.
Kauffman has done a fine job of making the patchwork structure fit the Encores! format of big band on stage, minimal scenery and scripts in hand as needed.
So we are left with a revival that captures Assassins’ smarts and musical brilliance, but ultimately, still lacks a certain something.
The production ends up being a bunch of pieces that look kind of ridiculous all put together.

It is an uneven production, marked by an oppressively downbeat mood in which the comedy is downplayed, puzzling directorial choices (ensemble members wearing prison-like jumpsuits, ritualistically pulling red ribbons out of a folded American flag), and performances that range dramatically in their effectiveness.
“Assassins” is also unsettling; more unsettling than entertaining...
John Doyle’s revival of the Sondheim-Weidman musical is well performed but brutally heavy-handed.
The result is cautious when it should be reckless, frigid when it should be sexy, and irked when it should be enraged.
It was the smartest and most devastating musical in town.
Assassins is quite the macabre framework for a somehow absolutely delightful musical.
“Assassins” may alternately delight you and appall you as you find yourself actually caring about some of the characters.
If you were ever curious about this show, seeing this cast in this production is probably your best bet.

cn.t: Critics find this timely revival of Sondheim's dark musical about presidential assassins eerily resonant post-January 6th, with an exceptional cast delivering the masterful score, though some find Doyle's minimalist staging heavy-handed or emotionally distant.
